verdict: The forecasting implementation is sound on the checks performed. The project still needs corrections and a completed submission package.

findings.title: Describe the test as retrospective, with prior exploratory exposure
findings.where: Slides 4, 8 and 10; report §4, printed p6 and §6.2, printed p9
findings.problem: Slide 8 calls the period unseen. Yet report §4 records 168 earlier Laya configurations evaluated on 2024–2025 and a TimesFM experiment covering 2019–2025. Also, the full 2023 validation results were unavailable at the earliest 2024 forecast origins. Publication lags do not reconstruct historical data vintages.
findings.why: A later configuration freeze fixes the final settings. It cannot make an already explored period untouched or make revised data historically available. This does not establish that the current finalists were chosen using test scores.
findings.fix: Use ‘retrospective chronological test’ in slide 8 and ‘assumed publication-delay conventions’ in slide 4. Add to report §6.2 and slide 10: ‘Earlier exploratory workflows had examined this period. Full-2023 validation outcomes and revised historical data were not all available at the earliest 2024 origins.’ Explain that the final specifications were fixed before their final comparison.
findings.accept: No claim of a pristine unseen holdout or fully reconstructed real-time information set remains. Report and slides disclose the same limits.

findings.title: Qualify validation conclusions by the metric used
findings.problem: ‘No developed model outperformed zero growth’ is true for primary RMSE, but not for MAE. Validation MAE is 1.0208424 for the fatality-conflict forest versus 1.0256610 for zero growth. That forest has worse RMSE.
findings.why: RMSE penalizes large errors more strongly. MAE and RMSE can rank the same forecasts differently. A result under one metric cannot be generalized to every metric.
findings.fix: Write ‘No tested developed specification beat zero growth on validation RMSE.’ On slide 7, specify that all four conflict forests worsened RMSE relative to the matched no-conflict forest. Keep MAE as the complementary measure.
findings.accept: Every universal validation ranking names RMSE. The group can explain why the chosen primary metric favors zero growth.

findings.title: Correct the retail-index base
findings.where: Report §2.2, printed p2 / physical PDF p3
findings.problem: The report says ‘January 2021 = 100’. The actual retail workbook metadata says ‘Index, 2021=100’.
findings.why: A base year and one base month are different definitions. This is a description error: constant rebasing cancels in the growth ratio, so the checked growth calculations remain valid.
findings.fix: Replace with ‘base year 2021 = 100’. Retain seasonally and calendar-adjusted volume and the food, beverages and tobacco scope.
findings.accept: Report metadata matches the supplied retail workbook.

findings.title: Correct the conflict-source chronology
findings.where: Report §2.4, printed p3; compare §3.2, printed p5
findings.problem: Section 2.4 describes annual data ‘as of 2023’ and monthly data ‘for 2024 and 2025’. The code uses annual GED v23.1 for training through 2022 and Candidate releases for both 2023 validation and 2024–2025 testing.
findings.why: Publication version, event month and forecast target month are distinct. The earliest Candidate reference file is November 2022, serving the assumed two-month-lag schedule for January 2023.
findings.fix: State: ‘Annual GED v23.1, covering events through 2022, supplies historical training exposure. Eligible monthly Candidate releases supply exposure for 2023 validation and 2024–2025 testing.’ Retain the annual-versus-preliminary source limitation.
findings.accept: Sections 2.4 and 3.2 agree with the model-panel provenance: annual 450, Candidate 60 validation, Candidate 120 test.
findings.basis: Source provenance and accurate method description

findings.title: Remove the unsupported COVID finding
findings.problem: Missing post-2022 coverage is described as having ‘added null predictive value’. This variable was not consistently evaluated over validation and testing.
findings.why: An unavailable variable is not evidence of a variable with zero predictive value.
findings.fix: Write: ‘We excluded COVID stringency because the imported series ends in 2022 and could not provide consistent predictors during validation and testing.’
findings.accept: The report describes a coverage-based exclusion and makes no untested predictive-value claim.
findings.basis: Distinguishing an empirical result from a data limitation

findings.title: Replace unsupported country classifications and exposure claims
findings.problem: The report calls Poland and Portugal ‘developing European economies’ and describes France/Germany as sufficiently distant from all conflict sources. The project does not establish these classifications or the asserted supply-chain/exposure ordering.
findings.why: These statements are unnecessary to the design and can undermine confidence in otherwise careful work.
findings.fix: Give a modest descriptive selection rationale: geographic and economic diversity among the five countries. Remove the categorical developed/developing and conflict-distance claims unless supported with appropriate evidence. Do not imply the five countries represent Europe statistically.
findings.accept: The sample rationale contains only supported factual descriptions and clearly acknowledges limited country coverage.

findings.title: Document the actual model controls and their rationale
findings.where: Report §4.3, printed p7; scripts/03_train_validate.R and scripts/00_config.R
findings.problem: The report mentions constrained complexity but does not give the principal numerical settings or clearly state fixed controls versus tuned optima.
findings.why: The course assesses justification of methods. ‘Forests did not help’ must mean these tested specifications, not every possible forest.
findings.fix: Add a compact specification paragraph or appendix. Forests: 500 trees, mtry = 2, maximum depth 5, minimum split node 40, minimum leaf 20, bootstrap replacement, sample fraction 1, one thread. Seeds are20564 plus forecast-month index, restarting at test. Describe the tree/bagging settings from stage 03 as well. State that these were fixed conservative controls, not exhaustive hyperparameter optimization.
findings.accept: A reader can identify the tested procedures without guessing and the group can explain their bias/variance tradeoff.
findings.basis: Syllabus method justification; Lesson 3 trees and ensembles

findings.title: Match the headline scope to the measured target
findings.where: Deck title and slide 2; report cover and business implications
findings.problem: FMCG is broader than the observed food, beverages and tobacco retail-volume series. Country-level monthly growth does not directly establish store/SKU-level inventory gains.
findings.why: The study evaluates an aggregate proxy. It does not evaluate the entire FMCG market or measure business savings.
findings.fix: Prefer ‘Forecasting monthly growth in food, beverages and tobacco retail volume’, or explicitly label the series as the project’s FMCG proxy. Keep operational benefits as motivation or possible uses requiring further validation.
findings.accept: Titles, question, target and conclusion share the same sector, geography and growth scope.

findings.title: Label error units and preserve the limits of inference
findings.where: Slides 6 and 8 RMSE tables; report §1.3; conclusion
findings.problem: The slide tables show RMSE without a unit. Wording about ‘no significant improvement’ can imply a statistical test that was not performed.
findings.why: The target is 100×log(index_t/index_t−1). MAE and RMSE are measured in log percentage points. An RMSE of 1.253 is not a 1.253% relative improvement. Small descriptive differences are not established statistically reliable or causal effects.
findings.fix: Add ‘RMSE in log percentage points’ below score tables. Keep improvement charts explicitly in percent relative to their named benchmark. State ‘Statistical significance was not assessed’ where needed. Retain the 24-month/common-shock caveat.
findings.accept: A reader can distinguish error units, relative improvement percentages and statistical claims.
findings.basis: Correct communication of metrics and uncertainty

findings.title: Close the ggplot2 installation gap
findings.problem: Setup checks only data.table/readxl. Stage03 handles rpart/ranger, but preparation calls library(ggplot2) without any install/check. README lists ggplot2 but provides no actual installation command.
findings.why: The project works in the tested installed environment but can fail early on a fresh machine. This is a concrete reproducibility gap, not a wrong forecast result.
findings.fix: Have the code owner include ggplot2 in setup, or give an explicit command before the master scripts: install.packages(c('data.table','readxl','rpart','ranger','ggplot2'), repos='https://cloud.r-project.org'). Keep one canonical run order. Preserve existing code comments when editing.
findings.accept: The documented setup accounts for all five dependencies, and the extracted final package runs both master commands in the intended environment.
findings.basis: Syllabus p5: required packages and reproducible top-to-bottom code

findings.title: Complete truthful contributions for all five members
findings.where: docs/CONTRIBUTIONS_TEMPLATE.md is still placeholders; author lists are not a contribution statement
findings.problem: The required brief statement of each member’s contribution is absent locally. The user confirms that work differed according to strengths and that all five were involved.
findings.why: The syllabus requires actual contributions, not identical roles or equal hours. A fair statement describes what each person contributed without inventing percentages or ranking people.
findings.fix: Create a short HTML contribution statement with each member’s confirmed tasks/deliverables and shared decisions. Suggested introduction: ‘Work was allocated according to members’ strengths. All five members contributed to the project.’ Describe shared final review only after it occurs. All five should verify the wording; then remove the blank template.
findings.accept: Every member has a truthful specific role description, everyone has reviewed it, and the completed statement is inside the final ZIP.
findings.basis: Syllabus pp5,7: contributions, fair participation and individual understanding

findings.title: Label historical freeze evidence separately from current results
findings.problem: The frozen score file preserves earlier forest numbers while current validation/test CSVs, figures and report use the reproduced local results. Candidate raw hashes also differ in bytes from the register because of CRLF versus LF line endings.
findings.why: Historical model-selection evidence should remain intact. It is not a current rerun score table. Line-ending differences alone are not changed data content. Fixed seeds do not ensure identical forests across software environments.
findings.fix: Label the frozen score file as historical freeze evidence and identify current CSVs as the numerical reference. Record the tested session/package versions. Document the Candidate line-ending normalization convention without modifying raw snapshots. Current forest GDP-removal improvement is 0.001117%, not the earlier 0.288894%.
findings.accept: One current result set feeds slides/report/figures; historical freeze values remain explicitly historical; no unexplained hash mismatch is presented as data corruption.

findings.title: Re-export and inspect the authoritative final PDF
findings.where: Big Data Working Paper.docx and Big Data Working Paper.pdf
findings.problem: The PDF is readable and has 10 physical pages. The Word file was saved later but access was denied to the audit tools, so Word/PDF parity could not be established. Timestamps alone do not prove the PDF is stale.
findings.why: The professor will grade the submitted PDF. Corrections in Word are ineffective if they are absent from that PDF.
findings.fix: Make the agreed corrections in the authoritative Word file, export the final PDF, then inspect all pages, equations, references and result numbers. Remove superseded submission copies once the final version is checked.
findings.accept: The actual PDF in the ZIP contains all agreed corrections and matches the final Word content. No Word-only correction remains.
findings.basis: Syllabus p5: technical report PDF; final deliverable integrity

findings.title: Show the evidence in a compact result table and a useful figure
findings.where: Current report has no tables or figures
findings.problem: The correct main results are buried in dense prose. The report gives little direct visual evidence of target behavior or country differences.
findings.why: The reader should be able to see the benchmark comparison and the limits behind the conclusion. The rules do not impose a chart count.
findings.fix: Add a compact six-finalist test table with MAE/RMSE, marking zero as validation-selected primary and country mean as the descriptive test winner. If space/time permits add the existing retail-growth history or country-comparison figure with a clear caption and brief description of variability/outliers. Use current saved results.
findings.accept: A non-specialist can locate the target, main comparison and conclusion without extracting numbers from paragraphs.
findings.basis: Syllabus clarity and data exploration; recommended, not a formal figure quota

findings.title: Finish the projection and editorial check
findings.problem: The independent rendering shows slide3’s title close to/overlapping ‘Predictors’, and dense charts/text on slides 6–9. Font-import warnings mean native PowerPoint must decide actual layout. Slide8 says ‘country meand’. XML also contains replacement characters in the slide6 model label, slide7 apostrophe/separators and slide9 apostrophe.
findings.why: Small plot labels and corrupted text make correct concepts difficult to understand. Import-render artifacts should not be mistaken for proven PowerPoint defects.
findings.fix: Fix the typo and replacement characters. Open the original in PowerPoint and the exported presentation PDF, check slide3 spacing and enlarge/simplify chart labels where needed. Verify country headings, error units and sources at projected size. The final deck has 11 slides including title and thanks.
findings.accept: No visible overlap/corrupted characters remain in native/exported output; audience can read the evidence from normal presentation distance.
findings.basis: Syllabus clarity; rendered preview finding requiring native verification

findings.title: Assemble, test, rehearse and upload the final package
findings.where: No correctly named final ZIP or upload receipt was available locally
findings.problem: A project folder is not proof of a complete submitted archive. The final package, successful extraction/run,15-minute rehearsal and actual upload remain unverified.
findings.why: A technically valid analysis can still lose marks through missing files or a broken handoff. User confirms the syllabus governs presentation length: 15 minutes. The old saved 10-minute guidance is unreliable and superseded.
findings.fix: Create exactly ‘20564 – Group Project – Group 02.zip’. Include final report PDF, final presentation, all R scripts, datasets or exact documented recovery sources and preprocessing, README, completed contributions and frozen configuration. Extract to a separate folder; follow the guide and check outputs against the reference scores. Rehearse for 15 minutes, agree speakers and ensure all members understand the core choices. Upload to the designated Google Drive Group Projects Submission Folder and verify the uploaded archive before 26 November at 16:00.
findings.accept: ZIP name, contents, extracted execution, 15-minute timing and Drive upload are all checked. Exclude temporary files, caches, old drafts and internal audit previews from the submission package.
findings.basis: Submission Guideline p1; syllabus p5; user-confirmed deadline and 15-minute rule
